title.en: Volume 452 Biographies 239: Hong Rukui, Yang Zonglian, Shi Pu, Shi Kekuan, Shen Baojing, Zhu Qiang younger brother: Qi Zhao, Zong Yuanhan, Xu Qingzhang, Xu Zhen, Kuai Guangdian, Chen Yusheng, Pan Minbiao, Yan Zuolin, Tang Xijin, Lou Chunfan
title.raw: 卷452 列傳二百三十九 洪汝奎 杨宗濂 史樸 史克宽 沈保靖 朱其昂弟：其诏 宗源瀚 徐庆璋 徐珍 蒯光典 陈遹声 潘民表 严作霖 唐锡晋 娄春蕃

sentences.zh: =洪汝奎=洪汝奎，字琴西，湖北漢陽人。

translations.literal: Hong Rukui. Hong Rukui, courtesy name Qinxi, was a native of Hanyang, Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Rukui. Hong Rukui, styled Qinxi, came from Hanyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-fourth year of the Daoguang reign (1844).

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，考取官學教習，期滿以知縣用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he passed the examination for Imperial College instructor; when his term ended he was appointed as a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng period he qualified as an Imperial College instructor and, upon completing his term, was selected for a county magistracy.

sentences.zh: 參曾國籓軍事。

translations.literal: He participated in Zeng Guofan's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Zeng Guofan's military staff.

sentences.zh: 同治初，洊保至江南道員。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, through repeated recommendations he rose to circuit intendant of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi years successive commendations advanced him to a Jiangnan circuit-intendant post.

sentences.zh: 總理糧台，供應防軍及他省協餉。

translations.literal: He superintended the grain bureau, supplying defense forces and assistance funds from other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the grain bureau, he supplied provisions for garrison troops and inter-provincial relief subsidies.

sentences.zh: 又籌還西征洋債，出入逾二千萬，綜核名實，不避嫌忌。

translations.literal: He also arranged repayment of Western-expedition foreign loans; receipts and disbursements exceeded twenty million; he audited names against facts and did not shun suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He also managed repayment of the foreign loans raised for the Western campaigns, handling more than twenty million taels in turnover while reconciling accounts rigorously and refusing to evade controversy.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，沈葆楨為兩江總督，尤倚任之。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, Shen Baozhen served as governor-general of the Two Jiangs and especially relied upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu, when Shen Baozhen governed the Two Jiangs, he leaned on him more than anyone else.

sentences.zh: 葆楨治尚威猛，因疾在告，輒疏請汝奎代治事，聲望益起。

translations.literal: Baozhen's governance favored stern severity; when illness obliged him to request leave, he repeatedly memorialized asking Rukui to administer affairs in his stead, and Rukui's reputation rose further.
translations.idiomatic: Shen governed in a stern, forceful style; whenever illness kept him on leave he repeatedly asked the throne to let Rukui act for him, and Rukui's standing grew accordingly.

sentences.zh: 會詔求人才，大臣交章論薦。

translations.literal: When an edict sought talented men, ministers submitted memorials one after another commending him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court called for talent, senior officials lined up to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 五年，特擢廣東鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was specially promoted to Guangdong salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was specially promoted to salt transport commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 調兩淮，裁冗費，建義倉，濬揚州城河。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Two Huai, he cut redundant expenses, established benevolent granaries, and dredged the Yangzhou city canal.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Two Huai salt administration, he pruned waste, founded charity granaries, and dredged Yangzhou's city canal.

sentences.zh: 方欲大有為，而江寧三牌樓之獄起。

translations.literal: Just as he intended great undertakings, the Nanjing Three Pailou case arose.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of major achievements when the Three Pailou case broke out in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 先是有棄屍三牌樓竹園旁，汝奎令參將胡金傳偵獲僧紹宗等仇殺謝姓男子，又稱薛姓，名亦屢易，汝奎請覆訊。

translations.literal: Earlier a corpse had been abandoned beside the bamboo garden at Three Pailou; Rukui ordered vice-commander Hu Jinzhuan to investigate and capture the monk Shaozong and others for having killed a man surnamed Xie in a vendetta; it was also said to involve the surname Xue, and the name changed repeatedly; Rukui requested a re-trial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a body had been found dumped near the bamboo grove at Three Pailou. Rukui had Vice-Commander Hu Jinzhuan trace the case to the monk Shaozong and others, accused of murdering a man surnamed Xie in a feud; the victim was also said to be surnamed Xue, and even his name shifted with each retelling, so Rukui asked for a rehearing.

sentences.zh: 葆楨以會匪自相殘，即置大辟。

translations.literal: Baozhen treated it as secret-society brethren killing one another and immediately imposed capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shen treated it as fratricide among secret-society members and had the defendants executed at once.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，得真盜週五、沈鮑洪等殺硃彪事，時地悉合。

translations.literal: More than three years later the true culprits Zhou Wu, Shen Baohong, and others were found to have killed Zhu Biao; time and place all matched.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years on, the real killers Zhou Wu, Shen Baohong, and others were caught for murdering Zhu Biao—the timing and location matched perfectly.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命尚書麟書、侍郎薛允升往江南即訊，金傳坐濫刑失入，治如律；

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Minister Lin Shu and Vice Minister Xue Yunsheng were ordered to proceed to Jiangnan for on-the-spot examination; Jinzhuan was convicted of improper punishment and wrongful conviction and punished according to law;
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Minister Lin Shu and Vice Minister Xue Yunsheng were dispatched to Jiangnan to reinvestigate on the spot. Jinzhuan was found guilty of abusive punishment and wrongful conviction and sentenced under statute.

sentences.zh: 汝奎失察，褫職遣戍；

translations.literal: Rukui was punished for failure of oversight, stripped of office and sent into exile;
translations.idiomatic: Rukui was punished for negligent supervision—stripped of office and banished.

sentences.zh: 葆楨以前卒，免議。

translations.literal: Baozhen had died earlier and was exempted from inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had already died and was spared further proceedings.

sentences.zh: 於是朝旨申戒各行省慎重刑獄，並禁嗣後武員毋庸會鞫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court ordered all provinces to take criminal cases seriously and forbade military officers thereafter from participating in joint trials.
translations.idiomatic: The court then warned every province to handle criminal cases with greater care and barred military officers from sitting in on civilian trials thereafter.

sentences.zh: 汝奎至戍所，未幾赦歸，遽病卒。

translations.literal: Rukui reached the place of exile; before long he was pardoned and returned home, but suddenly fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui reached his place of banishment, was pardoned and sent home soon after, but fell suddenly ill and died.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，總督端方疏陳其治行，復原官。

translations.literal: Early in Xuantong, Governor-General Duan Fang memorialized his administrative achievements and his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuantong reign, Governor-General Duan Fang memorialized his record in office and had his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: =楊宗濂=楊宗濂，字藝芳，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Yang Zonglian. Yang Zonglian, courtesy name Yifang, was a native of Wuxi, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zonglian. Yang Zonglian, styled Yifang, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐末，以戶部員外郎在籍治團練。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianfeng, as a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, he organized local militia while residing in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianfeng era, while holding a vice-director post in the Ministry of Revenue, he organized home-district militia from his native place.

sentences.zh: 時錢鼎銘乞師於曾國籓，宗濂偕行。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Dingming begged troops from Zeng Guofan, and Zonglian accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Dingming went to Zeng Guofan to request troops, Zonglian went with him.

sentences.zh: 及李鴻章以援師東下，宗濂率舊部為軍導，屢著戰績。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang led relief forces eastward, Zonglian led his old troops as army guides and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang marched east with relief forces, Zonglian led his former units as guides and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 劉銘傳進剿江陰，宗濂率濂字營守楊舍。

translations.literal: When Liu Mingchuan advanced to suppress Jiangyin, Zonglian led the Lianzi Battalion to defend Yangshe.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Mingchuan's campaign against Jiangyin, Zonglian held Yangshe with his Lianzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 賊來犯，宗濂領沙團擊卻之。

translations.literal: When rebels came to attack, Zonglian led the Sha Corps and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked, he led the Sha Corps and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 沙團者，起於江岸集眾自衛，以技勇名，賊皆畏之。

translations.literal: The Sha Corps had arisen along the riverbanks as people gathered for self-defense; famed for martial skill, all rebels feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Sha Corps were riverbank militia who had banded together for self-defense; famed for fighting skill, they were feared by every rebel band.

sentences.zh: 攻無錫，宗濂任前鋒。

translations.literal: In the attack on Wuxi, Zonglian served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Wuxi he commanded the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 與賊酋黃子澄鏖戰，夜奪北門入，拔其城。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely with the rebel chief Huang Zicheng, seized the north gate by night and entered, and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: He fought a pitched battle with the rebel leader Huang Zicheng, stormed the north gate by night, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 合攻常州，宗濂督戰西門，架浮橋，獨騎先進。

translations.literal: In the joint attack on Changzhou, Zonglian directed fighting at the west gate, erected a pontoon bridge, and advanced alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the combined assault on Changzhou he directed operations at the west gate, threw a pontoon bridge across, and rode ahead alone.

sentences.zh: 馬驚逸，墮河，躍起易騎再進，揮兵肉薄登，遂擒陳坤書。

translations.literal: His horse bolted in fright; he fell into the river, leaped up, changed horses and advanced again, waved his troops to close combat and ascend, and thus captured Chen Kunshu.
translations.idiomatic: His horse bolted and threw him into the river; he scrambled up, mounted another horse, pressed on, led his men in hand-to-hand fighting up the wall, and captured Chen Kunshu.

sentences.zh: 江南平，隨鴻章移師剿捻，總理營務處。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he followed Hongzhang in moving troops to suppress the Nian, and superintended the camp affairs office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified he followed Li Hongzhang against the Nian rebels as head of the camp affairs office.

sentences.zh: 軍興所至索官車，吏民交困，宗濂創立車營，行軍所需，預為儲峙，隨時無不備。

translations.literal: Wherever armies arose they requisitioned official transport, officials and people alike were distressed; Zonglian established a transport battalion so that what campaigns required was stored in advance and nothing was ever lacking when needed.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever armies marched they commandeered official carts and burdened officials and civilians alike; Zonglian created a transport battalion that stockpiled everything campaigns needed so supplies were always ready.

sentences.zh: 諸軍仿其制，皆稱便。

translations.literal: All armies imitated his system and all called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Other armies copied his system and found it indispensable.

sentences.zh: 積功擢道員。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Merit accumulated until he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，權湖北荊宜施道，被劾罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he acted as intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei and was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he served as acting intendant of the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei but was impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 鴻章創北洋武備學堂，奏起宗濂總其事，成材甚眾。

translations.literal: Hongzhang founded the Beiyang Military Academy and memorialized to recall Zonglian to direct it; many talented men were produced.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang founded the Beiyang Military Academy he had Zonglian recalled to head it, and the school turned out many capable officers.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年，授直隸通永道。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu he was appointed intendant of Tong-Yong circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu (1890) he was appointed intendant of the Tong-Yong circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔大潦，宗濂主賑事，假便宜發緡粟。

translations.literal: At that time the capital region suffered great flooding; Zonglian directed relief affairs and was granted discretionary authority to disburse silk funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region was stricken by severe floods, he directed relief work and was authorized to disburse funds and grain at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 復大治水利，修潮白、青龍、薊運、北運、通惠、永清各河。

translations.literal: He again undertook major water conservancy, repairing the Chaobai, Qinglong, Ji Canal, North Canal, Tonghui, and Yongqing rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He then launched a major waterworks program, repairing the Chaobai, Qinglong, Ji, North, Tonghui, and Yongqing rivers.

sentences.zh: 疏渠樹防，闢膏腴數万頃，士民刊碑頌德。

translations.literal: He dredged canals and planted dikes, opening tens of thousands of mu of fertile land; scholars and commoners erected steles praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: By dredging channels and building embankments he reclaimed tens of thousands of mu of rich farmland, and local gentry and commoners set up monuments in his praise.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 再起，為山西河東道，歷權布政使、按察使，遷長蘆鹽運使。

translations.literal: Recalled to service, he became intendant of Hedong circuit in Shanxi, successively acting as provincial treasurer and provincial judge, then transferred to Changlu salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to service, he served as intendant of the Hedong circuit in Shanxi, acted as provincial treasurer and provincial judge in turn, and was then appointed Changlu salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，聯軍犯天津，宗濂督蘆勇登陴固守，飛丸裂左脛，血流如沈，猶裹創治軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies attacked Tianjin; Zonglian directed Luzhou braves to mount the walls and hold firm; a flying projectile shattered his left shin and blood flowed like a deep pool, yet he still bound his wound and directed the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu (1900), when the allied armies attacked Tianjin, he led Luzhou militia onto the walls in a stubborn defense. A shell splinter shattered his left shin and blood pooled around him, yet he bandaged the wound and kept command.

sentences.zh: 城陷，巷戰，又傷右股。

translations.literal: When the city fell he fought in the streets and was wounded again in the right thigh.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he fought street by street and was wounded again in the right thigh.

sentences.zh: 命駐保定督糧台，旋隨鴻章入都議和。

translations.literal: He was ordered to garrison at Baoding and superintend the grain bureau, then soon followed Hongzhang into the capital to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Baoding to run the grain bureau, then accompanied Li Hongzhang to the capital for peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 事定，賞三品京堂。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was rewarded with third-rank metropolitan official status.
translations.idiomatic: When matters were settled he was granted third-rank metropolitan official status.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以病乞休，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he requested retirement on grounds of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to retire on grounds of illness and died.

sentences.zh: =史樸=史樸，字蘭畦，直隸遵化州人。

translations.literal: Shi Pu. Shi Pu, courtesy name Lanqi, was a native of Zunhua prefecture in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu. Shi Pu, styled Lanqi, came from Zunhua in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以進士用知縣，分廣東，歷惠來、乳源、南海等縣，所至有威惠。

translations.literal: As a metropolitan graduate he was appointed magistrate and assigned to Guangdong; he served in Huilai, Ruyuan, Nanhai, and other counties, winning awe and kindness wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate appointed magistrate, he was posted to Guangdong and served in Huilai, Ruyuan, Nanhai, and other counties, earning respect and goodwill everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 潮陽盜鄭段基殺前令，樸蒞任，立捕誅之。

translations.literal: The Chaoyang bandit Zheng Duanji had killed the previous magistrate; when Pu took office he immediately captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaoyang bandit Zheng Duanji had murdered the previous magistrate; as soon as Pu took office he had him captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 晉羅定知州，留省捕劇盜劉亞才及餘盜九百，並置諸法。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Luoding, he remained in the provincial capital to capture the notorious bandit Liu Yacai and nine hundred other bandits, all punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Luoding, he stayed in the provincial capital to round up the notorious bandit Liu Yacai and nine hundred accomplices, all of whom were punished under law.

sentences.zh: 粵省海盜久為患，樸航海往剿，降盜魁張十五仔等，盡散其黨數千，有不受撫者剿平之，擢知府。

translations.literal: Guangdong pirates had long been a scourge; Pu went to sea to suppress them, induced the pirate chiefs Zhang Shiwuzi and others to surrender, dispersed their parties of several thousand, and exterminated those who would not submit; he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long suffered from pirates; Pu took to the sea to suppress them, induced chiefs such as Zhang Shiwuzi to surrender, dispersed their bands of several thousand followers, and wiped out those who refused to submit, earning promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 剿英德土匪，遇伏佛岡，沒深澗，罣木得不死。

translations.literal: While suppressing Yingde bandits he was ambushed at Fogang, sank into a deep ravine, and caught on a tree to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: While campaigning against Yingde bandits he was ambushed at Fogang, fell into a deep ravine, and survived only by catching hold of a tree.

sentences.zh: 賊踵至，睨之，曰：「史公也！」

translations.literal: Bandits followed close behind, looked at him, and said: "It is Master Shi!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits caught up, looked him over, and cried, "It's Master Shi!"

sentences.zh: 爭引出，跪進飲食。

translations.literal: They vied to lead him out, knelt, and presented food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: They competed to escort him out, knelt before him, and offered food and drink.

sentences.zh: 樸責以大義，數且詈，誓絕粒。

translations.literal: Pu rebuked them with righteous principle, counting their crimes and cursing them, and vowed to take no food.
translations.idiomatic: Pu lectured them on duty and honor, listed their crimes and reviled them, and swore to take no food.

sentences.zh: 賊益敬畏，羅拜感泣，原縛渠自效。

translations.literal: The bandits grew still more in awe, bowed in rows weeping with emotion, and volunteered to bind their leaders and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were awed all the more, bowed in rows with tears, and offered to bind their leaders and serve under him.

sentences.zh: 會救至，舁之歸。

translations.literal: When rescue arrived they carried him back.
translations.idiomatic: When rescuers arrived they carried him home.

sentences.zh: 詔革職，仍令自效。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office yet still ordered him to redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed him from office but still required him to redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 匪平，復故官。

translations.literal: When bandits were pacified he was restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels were pacified he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 粵東匪起，省城戒嚴。

translations.literal: Rebels rose in eastern Guangdong and the provincial capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels rose in eastern Guangdong the provincial capital was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 守獵德砲台，連破沙灣、茭塘、新灶各賊巢，賞孔雀翎，知肇慶府。

translations.literal: He defended the Liede battery, successively broke the rebel nests at Shawan, Jiaotang, and Xinzao, was rewarded with a peacock feather, and appointed prefect of Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Liede battery, broke rebel strongholds at Shawan, Jiaotang, and Xinzao in succession, was awarded a peacock feather, and was appointed prefect of Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 梧州被圍，督兵往援，拔其眾還軍封川，且戰且守。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou was besieged he led troops to relieve it, withdrew his forces to Fengchuan, and fought while holding position.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhou was besieged he marched to its relief, withdrew his force to Fengchuan, and fought a holding action.

sentences.zh: 會英人陷廣州，大府不遑西顧。

translations.literal: When the English took Guangzhou the provincial authorities had no leisure to look westward.
translations.idiomatic: When the British captured Guangzhou the provincial authorities could spare no attention for the west.

sentences.zh: 樸與賊相持五閱月，大小數十戰，殺賊數千人。

translations.literal: Pu contended with the rebels for five months, fought several dozen battles large and small, and killed several thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Pu held the rebels at bay for five months in several dozen engagements and killed several thousand of them.

sentences.zh: 其後賊大至，會提督昆壽水陸並進，大戰封川江口，連捷殲賊，軍遂復梧州。

translations.literal: Later rebels came in great force; Regional Commander Kun Shou advanced by land and water together; a great battle was fought at the mouth of the Fengchuan River, successive victories annihilated the rebels, and the army then recovered Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels arrived in force, Regional Commander Kun Shou advanced by land and water, fought a major battle at the mouth of the Fengchuan River, won successive victories that destroyed the rebel force, and recovered Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉道員，再權肇羅道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to circuit intendant and again acted as intendant of the Zhao-Luo circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit intendant and again served as acting intendant of the Zhao-Luo circuit.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，移廣州，攝按察使，旋署糧儲道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he was transferred to Guangzhou, acted as provincial judge, and soon served as grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi he was transferred to Guangzhou, acted as provincial judge, and soon served as grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 樸在粵前後垂四十年，善治盜，尤善用人。

translations.literal: Pu spent nearly forty years in Guangdong altogether, excelled at suppressing bandits, and was especially skilled at employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Pu spent nearly forty years in Guangdong in all, was masterful at suppressing banditry, and above all knew how to use men.

sentences.zh: 南海隸為盜誣，特出之，後督捕得其死力。

translations.literal: A Nanhai subordinate was falsely accused as a bandit; Pu specially released him, and later when directing arrests the man served him with his utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanhai subordinate was falsely accused of banditry; Pu had him released, and the man later served him with unstinting loyalty in bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 撫瓊盜，易名入伍，多死敵。

translations.literal: He pacified Qiong bandits by changing their names and enrolling them in the army; many died fighting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Qiong bandits by enrolling them under new names; many died fighting for the government.

sentences.zh: 省圍乏餉，出勸募，立集百萬金。

translations.literal: When the provincial capital was besieged and funds were lacking, he went out to solicit contributions and immediately raised a million taels.
translations.idiomatic: When the besieged provincial capital ran short of funds, he went out to solicit donations and at once raised a million taels.

sentences.zh: 賊初起，獨主撫，及踞梧，則主剿，皆得其機宜。

translations.literal: When rebels first rose he alone advocated pacification; when they seized Wuzhou he advocated suppression—both at the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first rose he alone favored conciliation; once they held Wuzhou he favored suppression—in each case he chose the right moment.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，以籌解西征協餉，加鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, for arranging delivery of Western-expedition assistance funds, he was given the additional title of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu (1876) he was given the additional post of salt transport commissioner for arranging Western-expedition relief funds.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉重逢，賞二品服。

translations.literal: He again encountered the provincial examination cycle and was rewarded with second-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial examination cycle came round again he was granted second-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.

sentences.zh: =史克寬=史克寬，字生原，安徽六合人。

translations.literal: Shi Kekuan. Shi Kekuan, courtesy name Shengyuan, was a native of Liuhe, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kekuan. Shi Kekuan, styled Shengyuan, came from Liuhe in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，與兄克諧辦鄉團禦賊。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng he and his elder brother Kexie organized local militia to resist rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era he and his elder brother Kexie organized home-district militia against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 太湖陷，克諧殉。

translations.literal: When Taihu fell, Kexie died in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Taihu fell his brother Kexie was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 克寬從克太湖、宿松，解六合圍，以國子監典簿保知縣。

translations.literal: Kekuan followed in recovering Taihu and Susong, relieved the siege of Liuhe, and through recommendation as Imperial College assistant registrar was appointed magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Kekuan helped recover Taihu and Susong, lifted the siege of Liuhe, and was recommended from his post as Imperial College assistant registrar for appointment as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 同治初，劉銘傳剿捻，移征西回，皆挾克寬與俱，為司饋運及營務處。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, when Liu Mingchuan suppressed the Nian and then shifted to campaign against the western Muslims, he always took Kekuan with him, putting him in charge of supply transport and the camp affairs office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, when Liu Mingchuan campaigned against the Nian and then the western Muslims, he always took Kekuan along to run supply transport and the camp affairs office.

sentences.zh: 敘功，擢知府。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，李鴻章督畿輔，檄董工程局，掌河事，治滹沱，於獻縣硃家口闢減河三十里，循子牙河故道入海。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, when Li Hongzhang governed Zhili, he was ordered to direct the engineering bureau and manage river affairs; he regulated the Hutuo, opened a relief channel thirty li at Zhujia Mouth in Xian county, and followed the old course of the Ziya River to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu, when Li Hongzhang governed Zhili, he was put in charge of the engineering bureau and river works; he regulated the Hutuo, cut a thirty-li relief channel at Zhujia Mouth in Xian county, and sent the water to the sea along the old Ziya River course.

sentences.zh: 鴻章上其績狀，因奏任清河道，民立石頌其德。

translations.literal: Hongzhang reported his achievements and memorialized for his appointment as Qinghe circuit intendant; the people erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang reported his achievements and had him appointed Qinghe circuit intendant; the people set up a monument in his praise.

sentences.zh: 旋以他事被劾奪職，遂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached on another matter and stripped of office, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached on another matter, removed from office, and retired home.

sentences.zh: =沈保靖=沈保靖，字仲維，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Shen Baojing. Shen Baojing, courtesy name Zhongwei, was a native of Jiangyin, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baojing. Shen Baojing, styled Zhongwei, came from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年舉人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858).

sentences.zh: 父燿鋆，湖北通判，武昌陷，罵賊被害。

translations.literal: His father Yao Jun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao Jun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 保靖出入賊中覓遺骸，三載始得死事狀，得賜卹立祠。

translations.literal: Baojing went in and out among the rebels searching for the remains; only after three years did he obtain proof of death in service, and an imperial pension and memorial shrine were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Baojing moved in and out of rebel-held territory searching for his father's remains; only after three years did he secure proof of death in service, winning an imperial pension and a memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章督師上海，招參幕事，積功至道員。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang directed forces at Shanghai he recruited him to the staff; through accumulated merit he rose to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang commanded at Shanghai he recruited Baojing to his staff, and merit accumulated until he reached circuit-intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，授江西廣饒九南道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he was appointed intendant of the Guang-Rao-Jiu-Nan circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi (1872) he was appointed intendant of the Guang-Rao-Jiu-Nan circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時英使訂約煙台，議於江西湖口輪舟停泊起卸貨物，保靖以有礙九江關稅務，力爭之，總署卒廢約。

translations.literal: At that time the British minister concluded the Yantai treaty, proposing that steamships moor at Hukou in Jiangxi to load and unload cargo; Baojing argued that this would harm Jiujiang customs revenue and contested it vigorously; the Zongli Yamen ultimately annulled the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When the British minister concluded the Yantai treaty, its terms would have let steamships moor at Hukou in Jiangxi to load and unload cargo; Baojing argued this would harm Jiujiang customs revenue and fought the proposal until the Zongli Yamen annulled it.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，攝布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial judge and acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he was transferred to Fujian as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Guangxu (1881) he was transferred to Fujian as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 法越事起，方事急，城閉，錢米歇業，居民洶洶將為亂。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose, affairs were urgent; the city was closed, money shops and grain shops ceased business, and residents were in uproar about to riot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict broke out the situation was acute: the city gates were shut, money shops and grain markets closed, and the populace was on the verge of riot.

sentences.zh: 保靖出諭，發庫款三十萬以濟市面，人心始定。

translations.literal: Baojing went out to announce reassurance, disbursed three hundred thousand from the treasury to support the market, and popular sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Baojing went out to reassure the people, released three hundred thousand taels from the treasury to steady the market, and calm was restored.

sentences.zh: 以他事被劾奪職，旋复官，遂不復出。

translations.literal: He was impeached on another matter and stripped of office, soon had his rank restored, but thereafter did not return to service.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached on another matter and removed from office; though his rank was soon restored, he never returned to public life.

sentences.zh: 所著有讀孟集說、韓非子錄要、怡雲堂內外編等。

translations.literal: His writings include Expositions on the Mencius, Selected Essentials of Han Feizi, and the Inner and Outer Compilations of the Yiyun Hall, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings are Expositions on the Mencius, Selected Essentials of Han Feizi, and the Inner and Outer Compilations of the Yiyun Hall.

sentences.zh: =硃其昂=硃其昂，字云甫，江蘇寶山人。

translations.literal: Zhu Qiang. Zhu Qiang, courtesy name Yunfu, was a native of Baoshan, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qiang. Zhu Qiang, styled Yunfu, came from Baoshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治初，從軍攻南匯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he joined the army to attack Nanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he joined the campaign against Nanhui.

sentences.zh: 城賊原降，要一人入盟，無敢往者，其昂毅然請入受其降，城始下。

translations.literal: The rebels in the city wished to surrender but required one person to enter and conclude the pact; no one dared go; Qiang resolutely volunteered to enter and accept their surrender, and only then did the city fall.
translations.idiomatic: The besieged rebels offered to surrender on condition that someone enter the city to seal the pact; no one dared go until Qiang volunteered, entered, accepted their surrender, and the city then fell.

sentences.zh: 旋納貲為通判，累至道員。

translations.literal: Soon he purchased office as subprefect and rose through accumulation to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon purchased a subprefect post and rose step by step to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 北洋大臣李鴻章頗奇其才。

translations.literal: Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang greatly admired his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, minister for the northern coast, took a strong interest in his abilities.

sentences.zh: 福州船政造軍艦不適用，奏改商船。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou Naval Yard built warships that proved unsuitable, and a memorial was submitted to change to merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Warships built at the Fuzhou Naval Yard proved unsuitable, and the court was asked to shift to merchant shipping instead.

sentences.zh: 其昂與其弟其詔創議官商合辦，請設輪船招商局，鴻章上其事，遂檄為總辦。

translations.literal: Qiang and his younger brother Qizhao originated the proposal for joint official-merchant operation and requested establishment of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company; Hongzhang reported the matter and then ordered him as general manager.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang and his younger brother Qizhao proposed a joint official-merchant steamship company; Li Hongzhang memorialized the plan and appointed Qiang general manager.

sentences.zh: 御史董俊翰劾以力小任重，下鴻章查覆，仍力贊其成。

translations.literal: Censor Dong Junhan impeached him for bearing too great a burden with too little strength; the matter was referred to Hongzhang for investigation, yet he still strongly supported its completion.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Junhan impeached him for taking on more than he could manage; Li Hongzhang was ordered to investigate but still strongly backed the venture.

sentences.zh: 於是官商合力開局集股，並收並外人所設旗昌輪船公司以保航權。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials and merchants combined to open the bureau and collect shares, and also acquired and merged the Qichang steamship company set up by foreigners to protect navigation rights.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and merchants then opened the company, sold shares, and bought out the foreign-run Russell & Company steamship line to protect China's shipping interests.

sentences.zh: 數年，成效大著。

translations.literal: Within several years the results were greatly evident.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the results were striking.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，直、晉災，其昂輸私財力任賑撫，以勞致疾。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu, when Zhili and Shanxi suffered disaster, Qiang contributed private wealth and took full charge of relief, falling ill from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, when Zhili and Shanxi were stricken by famine, he spent his own fortune on relief work until illness overtook him.

sentences.zh: 鴻章特委權津海關道，越三日卒，詔優恤，贈光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Hongzhang specially entrusted him with acting as Tianjin customs intendant; three days later he died; an edict granted generous condolence and posthumously awarded Grand Secretariat Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang specially appointed him acting Tianjin customs intendant; he died three days later. The throne granted generous posthumous honors and the rank of vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其詔，字翼甫。

translations.literal: Qizhao, courtesy name Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qizhao, styled Yifu.

sentences.zh: 納貲為知縣，累至道員。

translations.literal: He purchased office as magistrate and rose through accumulation to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased a magistracy and rose step by step to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 歷充江、浙漕運事。

translations.literal: He successively served in grain transport affairs for Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly in Jiangsu and Zhejiang grain transport.

sentences.zh: 輪船招商局既成，復請以額定漕運費給輪船代為海運，局基始固。

translations.literal: After the China Merchants Company was established, he again requested that the fixed grain-transport quota be paid to steamships for sea transport in its place, and the company's foundation was then secured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the China Merchants Company was running, he secured the fixed grain-transport subsidy for steamship carriage by sea, giving the company a firm financial base.

sentences.zh: 再權永定河道，時出巡河堤上下，務盡其利弊。

translations.literal: He again acted as Yongding River intendant, often going out to inspect dikes up and down the river, striving to ascertain all advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as acting Yongding River intendant, touring the dikes up and down the river to learn every advantage and defect.

sentences.zh: 遇伏汛暴漲，嘗三晝夜不交睫，親督弁兵搶護，始免潰決，民皆德之。

translations.literal: When the summer flood season brought sudden rise, he once went three days and nights without sleep, personally directing officers and soldiers in emergency defense, and only thus avoided breach; the people all thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: During a sudden summer flood he once went three days and nights without sleep, personally directing emergency repairs, and averted a breach; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 擴充天津電報學堂，成材益廣。

translations.literal: He expanded the Tianjin Telegraph School and produced talent in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the Tianjin Telegraph School and turned out more graduates than ever.

sentences.zh: 時方議辦海軍醫學堂，其詔复捐自置天津法租界地四十畝為校址以成之，其急公好義類如此。

translations.literal: At that time a naval medical school was under discussion; Qizhao again donated forty mu of land he had purchased in the Tianjin French concession as the school site to bring it into being; his public spirit and love of righteousness were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: When a naval medical school was being planned, Qizhao donated forty mu he had bought in the Tianjin French concession as its site—typical of his public spirit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was posthumously awarded Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously made a Grand Secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: =宗源瀚=宗源瀚，字湘文，江蘇上元人。

translations.literal: Zong Yuanhan. Zong Yuanhan, courtesy name Xiangwen, was a native of Shangyuan, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuanhan. Zong Yuanhan, styled Xiangwen, came from Shangyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少佐幕，洊保至知府。

translations.literal: In youth he assisted on staffs; through repeated recommendations he rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served on official staffs and rose through successive recommendations to prefect.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，官浙江，歷署衢州、湖州、嘉興府事，敏於吏事，判牘輒千言。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he served in Zhejiang, successively acting in Quzhou, Huzhou, and Jiaxing prefectures; he was acute in administrative affairs and his case judgments often ran to a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he served in Zhejiang, acting in turn for the prefectures of Quzhou, Huzhou, and Jiaxing; sharp in administration, his written judgments often ran to a thousand words.

sentences.zh: 在湖州濬碧浪湖，興水利。

translations.literal: In Huzhou he dredged Bilang Lake and promoted water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In Huzhou he dredged Bilang Lake and promoted irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 時太湖漊港淤塞，前守楊榮緒疏濬無功，會有疏陳治法者，下郡，源瀚乃議大興工役，所規畫甚備。

translations.literal: At that time the Lou ports of Lake Tai were silted up; the previous prefect Yang Rongxu dredged without success; when someone memorialized treatment methods and the matter was sent to the prefecture, Yuanhan then proposed large-scale labor, his planning being very thorough.
translations.idiomatic: The Lou ports of Lake Tai were then silted shut; the previous prefect Yang Rongxu had dredged in vain. When a memorial on remedies reached the prefecture, Yuanhan proposed a major works program with meticulous planning.

sentences.zh: 榮緒回任，卒成之，補嚴州。

translations.literal: Rongxu returned to office and finally completed it; Yuanhan was transferred to fill Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rongxu returned and finally completed the project; Yuanhan was then appointed to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 兵後凋敝，多溫、台客民寄墾，習於剽劫，廉治其魁，遣散歸者六千人。

translations.literal: After the wars the region was depleted; many guest settlers from Wenzhou and Taizhou had come to reclaim land and were accustomed to plunder; he sternly punished their chiefs and sent six thousand back home.
translations.idiomatic: The region lay devastated after the wars; many settlers from Wenzhou and Taizhou had reclaimed land and turned to banditry. He punished their leaders and sent six thousand home.

sentences.zh: 治嚴五載，煦嘔山民，穿渠灌田，引東、西湖以洩新安江之暴漲，旱潦不害。

translations.literal: He governed Yanzhou for five years, warming and nurturing mountain folk, cutting canals to irrigate fields, drawing on the East and West Lakes to discharge the sudden floods of the Xin'an River, so that drought and flood did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he governed Yanzhou, caring for hill people, cutting irrigation canals, and using the East and West Lakes to discharge Xin'an River floods, so drought and flood did little harm.

sentences.zh: 每巡行田野，勸民力穡。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured the fields he urged the people to labor at farming.
translations.idiomatic: On his tours of the countryside he urged the people to work their fields diligently.

sentences.zh: 調寧波，通商事繁。

translations.literal: Transferred to Ningbo, where treaty-port affairs were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ningbo, where treaty-port business was heavy.

sentences.zh: 有戈鯤者，素豪猾，為英國領事主文牘，積為奸利病民。

translations.literal: There was one Ge Kun, habitually domineering and cunning, who served as chief clerk to the British consul and over time amassed illicit profits that harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Ge Kun, long domineering and cunning, served as chief clerk to the British consul and had amassed illicit profits at the people's expense.

sentences.zh: 源瀚發其罪狀，牒上大吏及南、北洋大臣，逐鯤海外。

translations.literal: Yuanhan exposed his crimes, memorialized to superior officials and the southern and northern coastal ministers, and expelled Kun overseas.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan exposed his crimes, reported him to superior officials and the coastal ministers, and had him expelled from the country.

sentences.zh: 法國兵船犯浙洋，源瀚從寧紹台道薛福成籌海防，多所贊畫，數有功。

translations.literal: When French warships violated Zhejiang waters, Yuanhan followed Ning-Shao-Tai intendant Xue Fucheng in planning coastal defense, contributing much counsel and winning merit repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: When French warships threatened Zhejiang waters, he worked with Ning-Shao-Tai intendant Xue Fucheng on coastal defense, contributing much sound advice and winning repeated credit.

sentences.zh: 晉道員，署杭嘉湖道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to circuit intendant and acted as Hang-Jia-Hu intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit intendant and served as acting Hang-Jia-Hu intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本構兵，調溫處道，沿海戒嚴，處以鎮靜，清內匪，捕誅盜渠十餘人，疆圉晏然。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Japan raised arms; he was transferred to the Wen-Chu circuit; the coast was placed under martial alert; he handled matters with calm, cleared internal bandits, captured and executed more than ten bandit chiefs, and the frontier remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu (1894), when Japan went to war, he was transferred to the Wen-Chu circuit. Though the coast was on alert, he kept order, suppressed internal bandits, executed more than ten ringleaders, and the frontier stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 又三年，卒於官。

translations.literal: Three years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 源瀚優文學，尤精輿地，所繪浙江輿圖世稱之。

translations.literal: Yuanhan excelled in literary studies and was especially expert in geography; the Zhejiang map he drew is praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan was accomplished in letters and especially skilled in geography; the map of Zhejiang he drew has been widely praised.

sentences.zh: =徐慶璋=徐慶璋，字興齋，浙江山陰縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Qingzhang. Xu Qingzhang, courtesy name Xingzhai, was a native of Shanyin county, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qingzhang. Xu Qingzhang, styled Xingzhai, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初佐都興阿戎幕，累保知縣，歷任奉天寬甸、蓋平、義州，晉興京同知。

translations.literal: At first he assisted on Du Xing'a's military staff; through repeated recommendations he became magistrate; he served in Kuandian, Gaiping, and Yizhou in Fengtian, and was promoted to subprefect of Xingjing.
translations.idiomatic: He began on Du Xing'a's staff, rose through recommendations to magistrate, served in Kuandian, Gaiping, and Yizhou in Fengtian, and was promoted to subprefect of Xingjing.

sentences.zh: 所歷多善政。

translations.literal: Wherever he served there were many good policies.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a record of good government.

sentences.zh: 常微行市中，遇有訟爭者，輒為剖其曲直而遣之。

translations.literal: He often went incognito in the market; when he met disputants in lawsuits he would straightway judge right and wrong and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: He often walked the markets in disguise; when he met litigants he would judge their disputes on the spot and send them home.

sentences.zh: 倡修養濟院，收養貧民。

translations.literal: He advocated repairing the poorhouse and taking in impoverished people.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted repair of the poorhouse and took in the destitute.

sentences.zh: 興俗春耕遲，慶璋集村氓語以農事不可違時之義，眾承其訓，有「早種一天早收十天」之諺，至今誦之。

translations.literal: The local custom was to delay spring planting; Qingzhang gathered village folk and spoke on the principle that farm work must not violate the seasons; the multitude accepted his teaching, and the saying "plant one day early, harvest ten days early" is recited to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom delayed spring planting; Qingzhang gathered villagers and taught that farm work must follow the seasons. The people took his lesson to heart, and the saying "plant one day early, harvest ten days early" is still remembered.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，由鳳凰廳調遼陽知州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he was transferred from Fenghuang subprefecture to be prefect of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu (1894) he was transferred from Fenghuang to be prefect of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 值中日戰亟，省東南各縣相繼淪陷。

translations.literal: It coincided with the urgency of the Sino-Japanese war; counties in the southeast of the province fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Sino-Japanese War was then at its height, and county after county in the province's southeast fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 僅遼陽為盛京門戶，賴先事籌備。

translations.literal: Only Liaoyang remained as the gateway to Shengjing, relying on prior preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liaoyang, the gateway to Mukden, held firm thanks to preparations made in advance.

sentences.zh: 募餉練兵，號鎮東軍，沿邊設防。

translations.literal: He raised funds and trained troops, styled them the Eastern Garrison Army, and set defenses along the border.
translations.idiomatic: He raised funds, trained troops as the Eastern Garrison Army, and fortified the border.

sentences.zh: 自遼陽而岫嚴、海城、复縣三千六百村士民，編團數万人，以遼南靦峒徐珍為練長，勒以兵法。

translations.literal: From Liaoyang through Xiuyan, Haicheng, and Fuxian, three thousand six hundred villages of gentry and commoners were organized into militia of tens of thousands; Xu Zhen of Miandong in southern Liaoyang was made drill leader and drilled in military methods.
translations.idiomatic: From Liaoyang through Xiuyan, Haicheng, and Fuxian he organized militia from 3,600 villages into a force of tens of thousands, with Xu Zhen of Miandong as drill leader, trained in military discipline.

sentences.zh: 日兵至，慶璋語眾曰：「敵迫矣！

translations.literal: When Japanese troops arrived, Qingzhang said to the multitude: "The enemy presses close!
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese troops arrived, Qingzhang told the people, "The enemy is upon us!

sentences.zh: 援師未集，汝等自為計，毋與我偕亡。

translations.literal: Relief forces are not yet gathered; you must plan for yourselves and need not perish with me.
translations.idiomatic: Relief has not arrived. Make your own plans; you need not die with me.

sentences.zh: 我死，分也！」

translations.literal: If I die, it is my portion!"
translations.idiomatic: If I die, that is my duty!"

sentences.zh: 眾感奮，皆請殺敵，遂迭敗日兵，俘百數十人。

translations.literal: The multitude were moved and inspired, all asked to kill the enemy, and thus repeatedly defeated Japanese troops, capturing more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by his words, they all asked to fight, repeatedly defeated Japanese detachments, and took more than a hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 戰守歷五越月。

translations.literal: Fighting and defense lasted through five months.
translations.idiomatic: They fought and held out for five months.

sentences.zh: 長順、依克唐阿方督戰，皆倚以為重，屢詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Chang Shun and Yike Tang'a were then directing the campaign and both relied on him as important; edicts repeatedly commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shun and Yike Tang'a, then commanding the front, both relied heavily on him, and the throne repeatedly commended his service.

sentences.zh: 是時州西連年水災，复募款捐濟，全活無算。

translations.literal: At that time the western part of the prefecture had suffered floods for successive years; he again raised funds for relief donations and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: The western part of the prefecture had suffered floods for years; he again raised relief funds and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 慶璋才而負氣，其平日為政寬猛兼施，眾畏之如秋霜，愛之如冬日，有徐青天之稱。

translations.literal: Qingzhang was talented and proud in spirit; in ordinary governance he combined leniency and severity; the multitude feared him like autumn frost yet loved him like winter sun, and he was called "Clear-Sky Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Talented and proud, Qingzhang governed with a mix of leniency and severity; the people feared him like autumn frost yet loved him like winter sun, and called him "Clear-Sky Xu."

sentences.zh: 如議成，擢甘肅慶陽知府，遷甘涼道，積勞致病，卒於官。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he was promoted to prefect of Qingyang in Gansu, transferred to the Ganliang circuit, fell ill from accumulated labor, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he was promoted to prefect of Qingyang in Gansu and then to the Ganliang circuit, but illness from overwork brought him to his death in office.

sentences.zh: =徐珍=徐珍，字聘卿，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhen. Xu Zhen, courtesy name Pinqing, was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhen. Xu Zhen, styled Pinqing, came from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 剛正多勇略，日軍犯遼，珍獨率民團守吉洞峪，扼險堅持，敵不得逞。

translations.literal: Upright and stern, full of courage and stratagem; when Japanese troops invaded Liaodong, Zhen alone led militia to defend Jidongyu, holding the strategic pass stubbornly so the enemy could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and resourceful, when Japanese troops invaded Liaodong he alone led militia to hold Jidong Pass, blocking the enemy at a strategic defile.

sentences.zh: 慶璋既屬以練長，會將兵者忌之，飭散團眾，防務遂弛，而吉洞峪鄉團之名，乃著於中外。

translations.literal: After Qingzhang assigned him as drill leader, commanders of regular troops grew jealous and ordered the militia dispersed; coastal defense then slackened, yet the name of the Jidongyu village militia became renowned at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhang had made him drill leader, but regular commanders grew jealous and ordered the militia disbanded, weakening the defense; yet the Jidongyu militia became famous at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 事定，以抗敵出力，保用縣主簿。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, for his exertions in resisting the enemy he was recommended for appointment as county registrar.
translations.idiomatic: After the war he was recommended for county registrar for his service against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，珍復辦民團，聯數百村，有匪即剿捕，不分畛域。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Zhen again organized militia, linking several hundred villages; wherever bandits appeared he suppressed and captured them without regard to boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer movement broke out he again organized militia across hundreds of villages and hunted down bandits wherever they appeared, regardless of jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 匪攻騰鰲堡及荒溝，先後剿平之。

translations.literal: Bandits attacked Teng'ao Fort and Huangou; he successively suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He successively suppressed bandit attacks on Teng'ao Fort and Huangou.

sentences.zh: 日俄之戰，珍嚴守中立，不稍假藉。

translations.literal: During the Russo-Japanese war, Zhen strictly maintained neutrality and gave no favor to either side.
translations.idiomatic: During the Russo-Japanese War he strictly maintained neutrality and gave neither side any advantage.

sentences.zh: 總督趙爾巽嘉珍功，以辦團成績上，有「上不支官款，下不取民財，徒以忠義之故，護衛鄉閭，保全無算」之語。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhao Erxun commended Zhen's achievements; in reporting his militia accomplishments he wrote: "He took no funds above from the government nor wealth below from the people; solely through loyalty and righteousness he guarded the villages and preserved countless lives."
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhao Erxun praised his militia work, writing that he "took no government funds above and no private levies below, but solely through loyalty protected the countryside and saved countless lives."

sentences.zh: 歷保至知府。

translations.literal: Through successive recommendations he rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive recommendations he rose to prefect.

sentences.zh: 武昌變起，土匪假革命名嘯聚煽亂。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang uprising broke out, bandits gathered and incited disorder under the false name of revolution.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang uprising broke out, bandits gathered mobs and stirred disorder in the name of revolution.

sentences.zh: 爾巽知珍義勇，委充巡防營

translations.literal: Erxun knew Zhen's loyal courage and appointed him to the patrol defense battalion
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhen's loyal courage, Erxun appointed him to the patrol defense battalion

sentences.zh: 幫統，分防遼陽、海城、岫岩、本溪四城，地方賴以安謐。

translations.literal: as assistant commander, dividing defense among Liaoyang, Haicheng, Xiuyan, and Benxi, four cities; the region relied on this for tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: as assistant commander, garrisoning Liaoyang, Haicheng, Xiuyan, and Benxi, on which the region's peace depended.

sentences.zh: 尋以巡防改編陸軍，遂辭職。

translations.literal: Soon the patrol defense force was reorganized into the regular army, and he then resigned.
translations.idiomatic: When the patrol force was reorganized into the regular army he resigned.

sentences.zh: 卒後，州人建專祠祀之。

translations.literal: After his death the people of the prefecture built a special shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of the prefecture built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: =蒯光典=蒯光典，字禮卿，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Kuai Guangdian. Kuai Guangdian, courtesy name Liqing, was a native of Hefei, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Guangdian. Kuai Guangdian, styled Liqing, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父德模，見循吏傳。

translations.literal: His father Demo is treated in the Biographies of Conscientious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: His father Demo has a biography among the conscientious officials.

sentences.zh: 光典幼慧，八歲能詩，隨父官江南，所師友多當代名儒，聞見日擴，名亦日起。

translations.literal: Guangdian was clever in youth; at eight he could compose poetry; following his father's office in Jiangnan, his teachers and friends were mostly renowned scholars of the age; his knowledge daily expanded and his fame daily rose.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious as a child, he was writing poetry at eight. Following his father to a post in Jiangnan, he studied with many leading scholars of the day, and his reputation grew steadily.

sentences.zh: 其論學務明群經大義，而以六書、九數為樞紐，治六書則必求義類以旁通諸學，識雙聲以明假借。

translations.literal: In his scholarship he sought to clarify the great principles of the classics, taking the Six Scripts and the Nine Numbers as pivot; in studying the Six Scripts he always sought semantic categories to extend to other learning, and recognized double initials to clarify loan characters.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he stressed the great principles of the classics, with the Six Scripts and mathematics as foundations; in philology he sought semantic categories to link the disciplines and used double initials to explain loan characters.

sentences.zh: 性強記，有口辯，尤熟於目錄掌故。

translations.literal: By nature he had a strong memory, skill in debate, and was especially versed in bibliography and historical anecdotes.
translations.idiomatic: He had a formidable memory, was a sharp debater, and was especially versed in bibliography and historical lore.

sentences.zh: 有所論難，援據該洽，莫能窮也。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered debate his citations were comprehensive and none could exhaust him.
translations.idiomatic: In debate his citations were so comprehensive that no opponent could exhaust his arguments.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the ninth year of Guangxu; appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Guangxu (1883) and was appointed a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 典貴州鄉試，與其副不相下，以狂倨見譏，然榜發稱得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Guizhou provincial examination; he and his deputy would not yield to each other; he was mocked for arrogance, yet when the list was published it was said he had obtained true scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As chief examiner for Guizhou he clashed with his deputy and was criticized for arrogance, yet when the results were announced he was praised for selecting true talent.

sentences.zh: 充會典館圖繪總纂，精密勝於舊。

translations.literal: He served as chief compiler of maps in the Collected Statutes Bureau; the precision surpassed the old.
translations.idiomatic: As chief map compiler for the Collected Statutes project, his work surpassed earlier editions in precision.

sentences.zh: 中東兵起，發憤上書，不報，遂乞假歸。

translations.literal: When war broke out in the Middle East he wrote in indignation to the throne; receiving no response, he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out he submitted an impassioned memorial; unanswered, he took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 總督劉坤一聘主尊經書院講席。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi engaged him to head the lecture chair at the Zunjing Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Kunyi engaged him to lecture at the Zunjing Academy.

sentences.zh: 光典念國勢弱，在列諸人惟鄂督張之洞有大略，又嘗所從受業師也，因往說之洞慎選才俊，習武備，為異日革新庶政之用。

translations.literal: Guangdian reflected that the nation's strength was weak; among those in office only Hubei Governor Zhang Zhidong had grand strategy, and he had once been his teacher; he therefore went to urge Zhidong to select talented youths carefully, study military preparedness, for use in future renovation of government.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the nation's weakness, Guangdian judged that only Hubei Governor Zhang Zhidong—once his teacher—had a broad vision, and went to urge him to select talented youths and train them in military affairs for future reform.

sentences.zh: 之洞韙之，卒不果，而聘為兩湖書院監督。

translations.literal: Zhidong approved the idea but in the end it did not succeed; he nevertheless engaged him as superintendent of the Liang-Hu Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang approved the plan but it never came to fruition; he nevertheless appointed Guangdian superintendent of the Liang-Hu Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，敘會典館勞，以道員發江南，創辦江寧高等學堂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year his Collected Statutes labors were recorded; he was dispatched to Jiangnan as circuit intendant and founded the Jiangning Higher School.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu (1898) his work on the Collected Statutes was recognized, he was sent to Jiangnan as circuit intendant, and he founded the Jiangning Higher School.

sentences.zh: 大學士剛毅按事江南，司道百餘人同詣謁，獨延光典密室縱談國事，語切直。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gangyi was inspecting affairs in Jiangnan; more than a hundred circuit and prefectural officials called together to pay respects; he alone invited Guangdian to a private room for free discussion of state affairs, his words blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Gangyi inspected Jiangnan, more than a hundred officials paid their respects together; he alone took Guangdian into a private room for a frank discussion of national affairs.

sentences.zh: 剛毅大憾，即議裁高等學堂。

translations.literal: Gangyi was greatly resentful and immediately proposed abolishing the higher school.
translations.idiomatic: Gangyi took great offense and immediately proposed abolishing the higher school.

sentences.zh: 光典力爭，不能得，拂衣去。

translations.literal: Guangdian argued strenuously but could not prevail and shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdian argued in vain and resigned in protest.

sentences.zh: 坤一兩解之，檄赴鹽城丈樵地，樵地者，故鹽場葦蕩也。

translations.literal: Kunyi twice mediated; he was ordered to Yancheng to survey firewood lands—lands that were formerly reed marshes of the salt fields.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi mediated twice and sent him to Yancheng to survey former salt-field reed marshes.

sentences.zh: 年餘得可耕之地七萬五千頃，收入荒價亦鉅萬。

translations.literal: In more than a year he obtained seventy-five thousand qing of cultivable land; revenue from wasteland prices also reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than a year he identified seventy-five thousand qing of arable land and brought in tens of thousands in reclamation fees.

sentences.zh: 領正陽關督銷局，歲增銷官引百數十萬。

translations.literal: He headed the Zhengyang Pass salt distribution bureau; yearly sales of official salt tickets increased by more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Zhengyang Pass salt distribution bureau he increased annual official salt sales by more than a million taels.

sentences.zh: 會之洞代坤一為總督，以江南財匱，用不足，議增貨釐。

translations.literal: When Zhidong replaced Kunyi as governor-general, because Jiangnan's finances were depleted and expenditures insufficient, there was discussion of increasing commodity transit dues.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong replaced Kunyi as governor-general, Jiangnan's treasury was empty and officials discussed raising commodity transit dues.

sentences.zh: 光典謂增新釐則病商，毋寧整齊鹽課。

translations.literal: Guangdian said that increasing new transit dues would harm merchants; better to put the salt tax in order.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdian argued that new transit dues would hurt merchants and that it would be better to reform the salt tax.

sentences.zh: 之洞因奏陳兩淮鹽事衰旺，謂：「北鹽視正陽銷數，南鹽視儀棧出數。

translations.literal: Zhidong therefore memorialized on the rise and decline of the Two Huai salt affairs, saying: "Northern salt is judged by Zhengyang sales figures, southern salt by Yizhan output.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang therefore memorialized on the Two Huai salt trade, saying, "Northern salt is measured by Zhengyang sales, southern salt by Yizhan output.

sentences.zh: 光典為江南治鹽第一，督正陽既有績，請使主儀棧。

translations.literal: Guangdian is foremost in Jiangnan for managing salt; since supervising Zhengyang he has already achieved results; I request that he be put in charge of Yizhan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdian is Jiangnan's foremost salt administrator; having succeeded at Zhengyang, I ask that he be put in charge of Yizhan.

sentences.zh: 期三年，成效必可睹。」

translations.literal: Within three years results will certainly be visible."
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the results will be plain."

sentences.zh: 詔允之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 光典既蒞事，以輪船駐大江三要區，首金、焦，次三江口，次沙漫洲，輔以兵艇，私梟斂跡。

translations.literal: Once Guangdian took office, he stationed steamships at three key points on the great river—first Jiao and Jin, next Sanjiang Mouth, next Shamanzhou—supported by armed boats, and private salt smugglers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he stationed steamships at three key points on the Yangtze—Jin and Jiao, Sanjiang Mouth, and Shamanzhou—backed by patrol boats, and private salt smugglers vanished.

sentences.zh: 始儀棧出數不足四十萬引，比三年，增引十餘萬，歲益課釐銀百五十餘萬。

translations.literal: At first Yizhan output was less than four hundred thousand tickets; compared with three years later, tickets increased by more than a hundred thousand, yearly revenue from tax and transit dues increased by more than 1.5 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhan output had begun below four hundred thousand salt tickets; within three years sales rose by more than a hundred thousand tickets, adding more than 1.5 million taels a year in tax and transit revenue.

sentences.zh: 乃益增募緝私兵隊，日夕訓練成勁旅，又於十二圩設學堂，建工廠，遂隱然為江防重鎮。

translations.literal: He then further recruited anti-smuggling troops, trained them day and night into a crack force, and also established a school and built factories at Shierwei, thus becoming covertly a major Yangtze defense post.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the anti-smuggling force, drilled it into a crack unit, and founded a school and factories at Shierwei, making the post a key Yangtze defense hub.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，按淮揚海道，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he inspected the Huai-Yang coastal circuit and was given the additional rank of provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Guangxu he inspected the Huai-Yang coastal circuit and was given the additional rank of provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 寶應饑民劫米，令潛逃。

translations.literal: Baoying famine victims looted grain; he ordered them to flee secretly.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying famine victims looted grain, he quietly had them dispersed.

sentences.zh: 適光典舟至，剴切諭解之。

translations.literal: Just then Guangdian's boat arrived and he earnestly admonished and dissolved the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdian happened to arrive by boat and earnestly talked the crowd into dispersing.

sentences.zh: 而揚州亦以饑民劫米告，诇知猾胥陰​​煽眾，即擒治胥。

translations.literal: Yangzhou also reported famine victims looting grain; he learned that a cunning clerk had secretly incited the crowd and immediately arrested and punished the clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou reported similar looting, he found a corrupt clerk had secretly stirred up the crowd and had him arrested at once.

sentences.zh: 大吏怒，將窮其獄，以光典言得免。

translations.literal: Superior officials were angry and were about to pursue the case to the end; through Guangdian's words they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Superior officials were furious and meant to prosecute the case to the end, but Guangdian's intervention spared the people further punishment.

sentences.zh: 運河盛漲，光典先分檄河員增修堤，而自泊舟高郵守視。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal rose greatly; Guangdian first sent separate orders to river officials to heighten dikes, while he himself moored his boat at Gaoyou to watch.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Canal flooded, he ordered river officials to raise the dikes while he moored at Gaoyou to supervise.

sentences.zh: 壩險工迭出，大吏以故事，視節候測水，檄啟壩，不為動。

translations.literal: Sluice emergencies arose one after another; superior officials according to precedent watched the season and measured water, ordering the sluices opened; he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: As sluice emergencies mounted, superiors followed precedent, measured the water by season, and ordered the gates opened; he refused.

sentences.zh: 歷月餘啟二壩，七月杪乃啟三壩，下河六縣獲有秋。

translations.literal: After more than a month two sluices were opened; only at the end of the seventh month was the third opened; the six lower-river counties obtained their harvest.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he opened two sluices, and only at the end of the seventh month the third; the six lower-river counties then brought in their harvest.

sentences.zh: 建言淮海災區廣，宜寬籌賑金，不宜設粥廠，使災民麕集，費不貲，且生事。

translations.literal: He proposed that the Huai-Hai disaster area was vast; relief funds should be broadly planned; soup kitchens should not be set up lest famine victims swarm together, costs become unpayable, and trouble arise.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Huai-Hai disaster zone was too vast for soup kitchens, which would draw starving crowds, waste funds, and breed disorder; broad cash relief would work better.

sentences.zh: 與布政使繼昌議不合，會奉檄入都參議改定官制，遂去任。

translations.literal: He disagreed with Provincial Treasurer Jichang; when ordered to the capital to discuss reform of the official system he then left office.
translations.idiomatic: He disagreed with Provincial Treasurer Jichang, and when summoned to the capital to discuss bureaucratic reform he left his post.

sentences.zh: 後江北賑事款絀而費糜，一如光典言。

translations.literal: Later northern Jiangsu relief funds ran short while expenses were wasted, just as Guangdian had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later northern Jiangsu relief funds ran short while expenses were wasted, exactly as Guangdian had predicted.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命赴歐洲監督留學生。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to Europe to supervise students studying abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu he was sent to Europe to supervise students abroad.

sentences.zh: 諸生不樂受約束，輒相訾謷，歲餘謝職歸。

translations.literal: The students disliked being constrained and constantly slandered one another; after more than a year he resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The students resented discipline and constantly quarreled; after a year he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 詔以四品京堂候補，充京師督學局長。

translations.literal: An edict made him a fourth-rank metropolitan official awaiting appointment and head of the capital school supervision bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a fourth-rank metropolitan official awaiting appointment and head of the capital school supervision bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，赴南洋提調勸業會，卒於江寧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he went south to direct the industrial exposition and died at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuantong he went south to direct the industrial exposition and died at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: =陳遹聲=陳遹聲，字蓉曙，浙江諸暨人。

translations.literal: Chen Yusheng. Chen Yusheng, courtesy name Rongshu, was a native of Zhuji, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yusheng. Chen Yusheng, styled Rongshu, came from Zhuji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the twelfth year of Guangxu; entered the Hanlin as bachelor; appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate in the twelfth year of Guangxu, he entered the Hanlin and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 出為松江知府，鹽梟久為患。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Songjiang; salt smugglers had long been a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Songjiang, he faced a long-standing salt-smuggling problem.

sentences.zh: 遹聲到官，密致其黨為導，帥健卒策疾騎踔百餘裡，掩其魁捕之，寘諸法。

translations.literal: When Yusheng took office he secretly sent his agents as guides, led sturdy soldiers on swift horses galloping more than a hundred li, surprised and captured the chief, and punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he sent agents undercover, led picked troops on a hundred-li forced march, surprised the ringleader, and executed him under law.

sentences.zh: 松窪下，數苦潦，濬支河三十餘，並籌歲修費數万金以澤農。

translations.literal: Below Songjiang the lowlands often suffered flooding; he dredged more than thirty branch canals and also planned annual repair funds of tens of thousands of taels to benefit farming.
translations.idiomatic: The lowlands below Songjiang flooded often; he dredged more than thirty branch canals and set aside tens of thousands of taels a year for upkeep to benefit farmers.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，暨俗素強，與教仇。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose, Zhuji custom was habitually strong and hostile to Christianity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer movement broke out, Zhuji folk were famously tough and hostile to missionaries.

sentences.zh: 不逞者轉相煽惑，眾至千餘，城鄉約期將為亂。

translations.literal: Restless elements incited one another; the crowd reached more than a thousand; town and countryside set a date to riot.
translations.idiomatic: Agitators stirred one another on until more than a thousand people in town and country fixed a date to rise.

sentences.zh: 遹聲獨命輿往喻之，途與眾遌，勢洶洶，斫輿前衡深寸許，正告之曰：「吾楓橋陳某也，來活爾！」

translations.literal: Yusheng alone ordered a sedan chair to go admonish them; on the way he met the crowd; the momentum was fierce; they chopped the front crossbar of the chair more than an inch deep; he solemnly told them: "I am Chen of Fengqiao, come to save your lives!"
translations.idiomatic: Yusheng alone went out in a sedan chair to reason with them. The mob was furious and hacked the chair's front crossbar nearly through. He called out, "I am Chen of Fengqiao, and I have come to save your lives!"

sentences.zh: 為指陳利害。

translations.literal: He pointed out advantages and harms for them.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out what they stood to gain and lose.

sentences.zh: 眾悟且泣，皆羅拜，爭棄械而走。

translations.literal: The multitude understood and wept, all bowed in rows, and vied to cast away weapons and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd understood, wept, bowed in rows, and threw down their weapons as they fled.

sentences.zh: 而城中莠民忽蜂起，遹聲促官守閉城，捕其魁五人斬以徇，事立平。

translations.literal: But bad elements in the city suddenly swarmed up; Yusheng urged officials to close the gates, captured five chiefs and executed them as warning, and the affair was immediately settled.
translations.idiomatic: Then ruffians inside the city rose; he had the gates shut, captured five leaders and executed them as a warning, and order was restored at once.

sentences.zh: 縣北江藻村，賭窟也。

translations.literal: Jiangzao village north of the county was a gambling den.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzao village north of the county was a notorious gambling den.

sentences.zh: 每歲十月，吳、越賭徒紛集，一擲累千金，破家者無算。

translations.literal: Every year in the tenth month gamblers from Wu and Yue gathered in crowds; a single throw could lose thousands of cash; families ruined were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Every October gamblers from Wu and Yue gathered; a single throw could cost thousands of cash and ruin countless families.

sentences.zh: 遹聲請於大吏，屆時縣官蒞村坐禁，著為例，數百年敝俗至此而革。

translations.literal: Yusheng requested of superior officials that when the season came the county magistrate should sit in the village to forbid it, establishing it as precedent; a corrupt custom of several hundred years was reformed at this point.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded superiors to require the magistrate to sit in the village each season and ban gambling by precedent, ending a centuries-old abuse.

sentences.zh: 服除，以勞遷道員，入參政務、練兵、稅務諸政。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to circuit intendant for his labors and entered into government affairs, troop training, and taxation.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was promoted to circuit intendant for his service and took part in government, military training, and tax affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授川東道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed to the Chuandong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu he was appointed intendant of the Chuandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 川東，盜藪也，蒞任未浹旬，開縣寇萬餘躪旁縣，立平之。

translations.literal: Chuandong was a bandit lair; within less than ten days of taking office, bandits of more than ten thousand from Kaixian trampled neighboring counties; he immediately pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuandong was bandit country; within ten days of taking office more than ten thousand rebels from Kaixian raided neighboring counties, and he suppressed them at once.

sentences.zh: 次年，黔中盜魁劉天成結蜀邊逋寇撓川南，防軍數為所敗。

translations.literal: The next year the Guizhou bandit chief Liu Tiancheng joined fugitive bandits on the Sichuan border to harass southern Sichuan; defense troops were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Guizhou bandit Liu Tiancheng joined Sichuan border fugitives to harass the south, repeatedly defeating government troops.

sentences.zh: 省檄練軍七營剿之，寇至，委械去。

translations.literal: The province ordered seven battalions of trained troops to suppress them; when the bandits arrived they abandoned weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The province sent seven trained battalions against them, but when the bandits appeared the troops dropped their arms and fled.

sentences.zh: 遹聲立募精勇數百人，部以兵法，疾馳赴援，未匝月，生縛天成歸。
