translations.literal: Yusheng immediately recruited several hundred picked braves, organized them by military methods, galloped to relieve, and within less than a month captured Tiancheng alive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yusheng raised several hundred picked men, drilled them in military discipline, rushed to the rescue, and within a month captured Tiancheng alive.

sentences.zh: 江北廳產煤，礦衇綿延數百里，至合州。

translations.literal: Jiangbei subprefecture produced coal; the veins extended several hundred li to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangbei subprefecture had coal seams stretching several hundred li to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 奸民私售龍王洞於英商，外務部與訂租約，胥江北廳礦產授之；

translations.literal: Wicked men privately sold Dragon King Cave to British merchants; the Foreign Ministry concluded a lease and handed over all Jiangbei subprefecture mineral rights;
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt locals secretly sold Dragon King Cave to British merchants; the Foreign Ministry signed a lease handing over all Jiangbei mineral rights;

sentences.zh: 复要展拓至石牛溝，且蔓及兩川。

translations.literal: they further demanded extension to Shiniugou and encroachment on both Sichuans.
translations.idiomatic: and the British also demanded extension to Shiniugou, encroaching on both provinces.

sentences.zh: 川人憤，將與英商角。

translations.literal: Sichuan people were enraged and were about to clash with British merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan people were furious and on the verge of fighting the British.

sentences.zh: 遹聲力爭之英領事，並密囑川人收石牛溝左右地。

translations.literal: Yusheng argued strenuously with the British consul and secretly instructed Sichuan people to buy up land around Shiniugou.
translations.idiomatic: Yusheng fought the case before the British consul and secretly urged Sichuan people to buy up land around Shiniugou.

sentences.zh: 英商以無佗地可得，得溝與洞，猶石田也，恫喝百端，不為動，卒以賤值贖回。

translations.literal: British merchants, finding no other land obtainable, though they had the gully and cave—still barren fields—threatened in every way but he did not budge, and in the end bought them back at a low price.
translations.idiomatic: With no other land available the British held the gully and cave—worthless ground—and tried every threat, but he stood firm until they sold the rights back cheaply.

sentences.zh: 治渝兩載，大吏交章論薦，遽引疾歸。

translations.literal: After governing Chongqing for two years, superior officials submitted memorials commending him one after another, but he suddenly cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in Chongqing, with superiors lining up to recommend him, he suddenly pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 當軸數招之，謝不出。

translations.literal: Those in power repeatedly summoned him; he declined and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power summoned him repeatedly, but he refused to return.

sentences.zh: 著有明逸民詩、畸廬稗說及詩集等。

translations.literal: His writings include Poems of Ming Recluses, Miscellanies of the Qilu Studio, and collected poems, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings are Poems of Ming Recluses, Miscellanies of the Qilu Studio, and collected verse.

sentences.zh: =潘民表=潘民表，字振聲，江蘇陽湖人。

translations.literal: Pan Minbiao. Pan Minbiao, courtesy name Zhensheng, was a native of Yanghu, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Minbiao. Pan Minbiao, styled Zhensheng, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治十二年舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twelfth year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twelfth year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，數募金賑直隸、河南、山西諸行省。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he repeatedly raised funds to relieve Zhili, Henan, Shanxi, and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he repeatedly raised relief funds for Zhili, Henan, Shanxi, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 十五年，山東河決，凡賑歷城、齊河、臨邑、齊東、濟陽、惠民、商河、青城、濱、霑化、海豐、陽信、蒲台十三州縣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Yellow River burst its banks in Shandong; he relieved altogether Licheng, Qihe, Linyi, Qidong, Jiyang, Huimin, Shanghe, Qingcheng, Bin, Zhanhua, Haifeng, Yangxin, and Putai—thirteen prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu the Yellow River broke its banks in Shandong; he directed relief in thirteen prefectures and counties including Licheng, Qihe, Linyi, and Putai.

sentences.zh: 閱四年始竣。

translations.literal: After four years it was finally completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work took four years to complete.

sentences.zh: 災​​民無歸者眾，民表於歷城臥牛山建屋五百間、窩棚千間居之，使植桑麻，興耕織，疾病婚嫁，皆有資助。

translations.literal: Many disaster victims had nowhere to return; Minbiao at Woniushan in Licheng built five hundred rooms and a thousand sheds to house them, had them plant mulberry and hemp, promote farming and weaving, and provided aid for illness and marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Many victims had nowhere to go; at Woniushan in Licheng he built five hundred houses and a thousand sheds, set them to mulberry planting and weaving, and aided them in sickness and marriage.

sentences.zh: 別建工廠百間，義塾八所，設教養局董之。

translations.literal: He separately built a hundred workshops and eight charity schools, establishing a nurture-and-education bureau to direct them.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a hundred workshops and eight charity schools under a nurture-and-education bureau.

sentences.zh: 因其規畫，歷十年之久，多有藝成自給者，乃以經費改設蒙養學堂。

translations.literal: According to his planning, over ten years many became skilled and self-supporting; the funds were then converted to establish an elementary school.
translations.idiomatic: Under his plan, within ten years many became self-supporting through craft skills, and the funds were then turned into an elementary school.

sentences.zh: 十九年，賑山西大同邊外豐鎮諸廳，亦仿臥牛山成法，收集教養之，尋以州同就職山東，署恩縣，補平度，擢泰安知府。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he relieved Fengzhen and other banners beyond Datong in Shanxi, likewise following the Woniushan method to gather and nurture victims; soon he took office in Shandong as subprefect, acted in En county, filled Pingdu, and was promoted to prefect of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he relieved Fengzhen and other banners beyond Datong using the Woniushan model, then entered Shandong service as subprefect, acted in En county, filled Pingdu, and rose to prefect of Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，河決利津，詔頒內帑十萬，大吏檄民表去任專賑事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the river burst at Lijin; an edict issued a hundred thousand from the privy purse; superior officials ordered Minbiao to leave office and devote himself solely to relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the river broke at Lijin; the throne allotted a hundred thousand taels from the privy purse and ordered Minbiao to leave office for full-time relief work.

sentences.zh: 晉道員，發陝西，筦農工商礦局。

translations.literal: He was promoted to circuit intendant, dispatched to Shaanxi, and managed the bureau of agriculture, industry, commerce, and mining.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to circuit intendant, he was sent to Shaanxi to head the bureau of agriculture, industry, commerce, and mining.

sentences.zh: 民表諗同官縣土質宜磁，建磁窯同官，興大利。

translations.literal: Minbiao knew Tongguan county's soil suited porcelain; he built porcelain kilns at Tongguan and developed great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Tongguan county's soil suited porcelain, he built kilns there to great profit.

sentences.zh: 貲竭將中輟，請兼盩厔釐榷，以羨餘助磁業，仍不給，且虧稅，計無所出，竟仰藥死，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Funds were exhausted and the venture about to halt; he requested also to take charge of Zhouzhi transit dues, using surplus to aid the porcelain industry; still it was insufficient, and taxes were lost; with no plan he finally took poison and died; public opinion mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When funds ran out he asked to take Zhouzhi transit dues as well to subsidize the kilns, but revenue still fell short and taxes were lost; with no way out he took poison, to widespread regret.

sentences.zh: 民表瘁於賑務二十餘年，每遇災祲，呼籲奔走，置身家不顧，敝衣草履，躑躅泥塗，面目黧黑，非人所堪，貲斧悉自貸。

translations.literal: Minbiao wore himself out in relief work for more than twenty years; whenever disaster struck he cried out and rushed about, heedless of family, in worn clothes and straw sandals, trudging through mud, face darkened beyond what men can bear; all expenses he borrowed himself.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years Minbiao wore himself out in relief work; at every disaster he rushed about heedless of family, in rags and straw sandals through the mud, his face blackened with hardship, borrowing every penny himself.

sentences.zh: 及服官，俸入悉以償賑債，充賑用。

translations.literal: When he took office his salary all went to repay relief debts and fund relief.
translations.idiomatic: In office his entire salary went to repay relief debts and fund more relief.

sentences.zh: 自義賑風起，或從事數年，由寒儒而致素豐。

translations.literal: Since the rise of charitable relief, some worked several years and went from poor scholar to great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Since charitable relief became fashionable, some poor scholars grew rich after a few years' work.

sentences.zh: 如民表之始終無染，歿無餘貲者，蓋不數覯。

translations.literal: Such as Minbiao, unstained from start to finish, dying without surplus wealth, are rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Minbiao, unstained throughout and dying penniless, were rare indeed.

sentences.zh: =嚴作霖=嚴作霖，字佑之，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Yan Zuolin. Yan Zuolin, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuolin. Yan Zuolin, styled Youzhi, came from Dantu.

sentences.zh: 以儒生奮起司賑事。

translations.literal: As a Confucian scholar he rose up to direct relief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucian scholar, he threw himself into directing relief.

sentences.zh: 自光緒二年始至三十年，歷賑山東、河南、山西、安徽、江蘇、直隸、廣西、奉天、陝西數行省。

translations.literal: From the second year of Guangxu to the thirtieth he relieved Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhili, Guangxi, Fengtian, Shaanxi, and several other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: From the second to the thirtieth year of Guangxu he directed relief in Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhili, Guangxi, Fengtian, Shaanxi, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 每兼濬河修堤，以工代賑。

translations.literal: Each time he also dredged rivers and repaired dikes, using labor for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He usually combined river dredging and dike repair with work-relief.

sentences.zh: 作霖性強毅，赴事勇決，綜覈無糜費，久而為人所信，故樂輸者眾。

translations.literal: Zuolin was strong and resolute by nature, bold and decisive in action, comprehensive in audit without waste; over time people trusted him, so donors were many.
translations.idiomatic: Resolute and decisive, he audited accounts without waste; over time donors trusted him and gave generously.

sentences.zh: 其施賑不拘成法，隨時地而取其宜。

translations.literal: His relief did not cling to fixed methods but took what was suitable to time and place.
translations.idiomatic: He did not cling to fixed methods but adapted relief to time and place.

sentences.zh: 當時疆吏以義賑可矯官吏拘牽延緩積習，樂倚以集事。

translations.literal: Border officials of the time regarded charitable relief as able to correct officials' habit of constraint, delay, and procrastination, and gladly relied on it to accomplish tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials found charitable relief could break bureaucratic delay and gladly relied on men like him to get things done.

sentences.zh: 作霖不求仕進，輒辭薦剡，僅受國子監助教銜，數被溫詔嘉焉。

translations.literal: Zuolin did not seek advancement, always declining recommendations, accepting only the rank of Imperial College assistant instructor, and was repeatedly commended by warm edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He sought no office, always declined recommendations, accepted only the rank of Imperial College assistant instructor, and received repeated warm commendations from the throne.

sentences.zh: 積賑餘貲興揚州、鎮江兩郡善舉。

translations.literal: He accumulated relief surplus funds to promote charitable works in Yangzhou and Zhenjiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He used relief surpluses to fund charity in Yangzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 及歿，子良沛出二十餘萬金為卹嫠、保節、備荒等用，成其遺志雲。

translations.literal: After his death his son Liangpei contributed more than two hundred thousand taels for widows' relief, chastity preservation, famine reserve, and other uses, fulfilling his last wishes.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Liangpei gave more than two hundred thousand taels for widows, chastity awards, and famine reserves, fulfilling his wishes.

sentences.zh: =唐錫晉=唐錫晉，字桐卿，無錫人。

translations.literal: Tang Xijin. Tang Xijin, courtesy name Tongqing, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xijin. Tang Xijin, styled Tongqing, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 父文源，闔門殉粵難，積尸滿井。

translations.literal: His father Wenyuan, the whole household martyred in the Guangdong calamity, corpses piled filling the well.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenyuan and the entire household died in the Guangdong rebellion; corpses filled their well.

sentences.zh: 亂平，錫晉拾親骨，瀝血取驗，誓奉遺訓力行善。

translations.literal: When the turmoil subsided Xijin gathered his family's bones, strained blood for verification, and vowed to follow his father's last instruction and strive in doing good.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned he gathered his family's bones, verified them by blood, and vowed to follow his father's last charge to do good.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，聞豫、晉災，始募義賑。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu, hearing of disasters in Henan and Shanxi, he first raised charitable relief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, hearing of famine in Henan and Shanxi, he began charitable relief work.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以恩貢授安東縣教諭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as a tribute student by grace he was appointed instructor of Andong county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he was appointed instructor of Andong county as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 時淮、徐、海大水，錫晉棹小舟往賑，憂勞甚，鬚髮為白。

translations.literal: At that time Huai, Xu, and Hai suffered great floods; Xijin poled a small boat to relieve them; his worry and labor were extreme and his beard and hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai, Xu, and Hai were flooded he poled a small boat through the waters on relief work until his hair turned white from strain.

sentences.zh: 明年，安東澇，益募金賑之。

translations.literal: The next year Andong was waterlogged; he further raised funds to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Andong flooded again, he raised more funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 冬，复賑山東沿海諸郡災，為置常平倉。

translations.literal: In winter he again relieved disasters in Shandong coastal prefectures and established ever-normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he relieved the Shandong coast and established ever-normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮西狩，關中大饑，人相食，錫晉醵金四十萬往賑，歷二州八縣，艱困不少阻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the two palaces went west on hunt; Guanzhong suffered great famine and men ate one another; Xijin collected four hundred thousand taels and went to relieve, passing through two prefectures and eight counties, hardships not slightly hindering him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the court fled west and Guanzhong faced famine so severe that people ate one another, he raised four hundred thousand taels and crossed two prefectures and eight counties without flinching.

sentences.zh: 災​​區廣，賑款且匱，乃單車詣行在，請於大學士王文韶，得二十萬金益之。

translations.literal: The disaster area was vast and relief funds were running short; he went alone by cart to the traveling palace, requested from Grand Secretary Wang Wenshao, and obtained two hundred thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: When funds ran short he traveled alone to the court in exile and secured another two hundred thousand taels from Grand Secretary Wang Wenshao.

sentences.zh: 事竣，返安東。

translations.literal: When affairs were concluded he returned to Andong.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he returned to Andong.

sentences.zh: 坐劾安東知縣貪殘，同落職。

translations.literal: For impeaching the Andong magistrate as greedy and cruel he was likewise removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office along with the Andong magistrate he had impeached for greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督端方等奏复錫晉官，改銓長洲，後​​以輸金助賑保道員。

translations.literal: Two Jiangs Governor-General Duan Fang and others memorialized to restore Xijin's office; he was reassigned to Changzhou; later for contributing funds to aid relief he was secured promotion to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Duan Fang had his office restored and reassigned him to Changzhou; later he was promoted to circuit intendant for contributing to relief.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，湘中災，官紳復以賑事囑。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Hunan suffered disaster; officials and gentry again entrusted relief affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, when Hunan was stricken, officials and gentry again put him in charge of relief.

sentences.zh: 秋，淮浦被水，流民數十萬洶聚，喻遣勿散，咸曰：「有司行賑不足恃，必得唐公。」

translations.literal: In autumn the Huai coast was inundated; several hundred thousand refugees gathered in uproar; admonished to disperse they would not; all said: "Official relief cannot be relied on; we must have Master Tang."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn floods on the Huai coast drove hundreds of thousands of refugees together; though told to disperse they refused, saying, "Official relief cannot be trusted—we must have Master Tang."

sentences.zh: 時錫晉臥病，猶強扶而至，眾見其來，驩曰：「吾生矣！」

translations.literal: At that time Xijin lay ill but still forced himself to come; when the multitude saw him arrive they rejoiced: "We shall live!"
translations.idiomatic: Though ill in bed, he forced himself to come; when the crowd saw him they cried, "We are saved!"

sentences.zh: 乃各還歸待賑，遂以無事。

translations.literal: Thereupon each returned home to await relief, and thus there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: They went home to await relief, and trouble was averted.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，方籌賑江、皖，而武昌變起。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong he was just planning relief for Jiangsu and Anhui when the Wuchang uprising broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuantong he was planning relief for Jiangsu and Anhui when the Wuchang uprising broke out.

sentences.zh: 錫晉憂憤，病日劇，越歲卒。

translations.literal: Xijin was grieved and indignant; his illness daily worsened; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and anger worsened his illness, and he died the following year.

sentences.zh: 錫晉治賑，自乙亥至辛亥，凡三十有七年，其賑地為行省八：山西、河南、江蘇、山東以及陝西、湖南，東至吉林，西至甘肅；

translations.literal: Xijin directed relief from yihai to xinhai, altogether thirty-seven years; his relief areas were eight provinces: Shanxi, Henan, Jiangsu, Shandong, as well as Shaanxi and Hunan, east to Jilin, west to Gansu;
translations.idiomatic: Xijin directed relief for thirty-seven years from 1875 to 1911 across eight provinces—Shanxi, Henan, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shaanxi, and Hunan, from Jilin in the east to Gansu in the west;

sentences.zh: 其賑款過百萬以上。

translations.literal: his relief funds exceeded more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: and his relief funds exceeded a million taels.

sentences.zh: 義賑之遠且久，無過錫晉。

translations.literal: In charitable relief for distance and duration none surpassed Xijin.
translations.idiomatic: No charitable relief effort matched his in scope or duration.

sentences.zh: 歿後眾思其德，受賑各省咸請立祠祀之。

translations.literal: After his death the multitude remembered his virtue; all provinces that had received relief requested shrines to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death every province he had helped asked to build a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: =婁春蕃=婁春蕃，字椒生，浙江紹興人。

translations.literal: Lou Chunfan. Lou Chunfan, courtesy name Jiaosheng, was a native of Shaoxing, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Chunfan. Lou Chunfan, styled Jiaosheng, came from Shaoxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以貢生納貲為同知，歷保道員。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he purchased office as subprefect and through recommendations rose to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute student who purchased a subprefect post, he rose through recommendations to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 久參北洋幕府，李鴻章尤重之，常倚以治繁劇。

translations.literal: He long served on the Beiyang staff; Li Hongzhang especially valued him and often relied on him to handle difficult and urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He long served on the Beiyang staff; Li Hongzhang valued him highly and often relied on him for the hardest assignments.

sentences.zh: 春蕃熟諳直隸水利，永定河常歲決，思患預防，以時消息之，河不數病。

translations.literal: Chunfan was well versed in Zhili water conservancy; the Yongding River often burst yearly; he thought of disaster and took preventive measures, regulating it according to season, and the river did not frequently cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfan knew Zhili waterworks thoroughly; though the Yongding River breached almost every year, he anticipated trouble, regulated the flow by season, and kept disasters rare.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽商久困增釐，春蕃務為寬大，課裕而商不撓。

translations.literal: Changlu salt merchants had long been distressed by increased transit dues; Chunfan strove for leniency; tax revenue was ample yet merchants were not harassed.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu salt merchants had long suffered under added transit dues; Chunfan pursued a lenient policy so revenue stayed strong without harassing the trade.

sentences.zh: 尤精刑律，審覈維慎，直省遂無冤獄。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in penal law, cautious in review, and thus the metropolitan province had no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in penal law and meticulous in review, he kept wrongful convictions out of the metropolitan province.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，力主剿辦。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose he strongly advocated suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer movement broke out he strongly favored military suppression.

sentences.zh: 為總督裕祿草奏，痛陳邪術萬不可信，戰釁萬不可開，以一服八，決無幸理。

translations.literal: He drafted a memorial for Governor-General Yulu, bitterly stating that heterodox arts were utterly untrustworthy, war must not be opened, one against eight had no chance of success.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a memorial for Governor-General Yulu arguing that Boxer magic was worthless, war must be avoided, and one power against eight could not possibly win.

sentences.zh: 裕祿初頗信之，不能堅持，卒致敗裂。

translations.literal: Yulu at first believed him somewhat but could not hold firm, and in the end met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yulu initially listened but could not hold the line, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 匪以通敵誣紳富，請搜殺。

translations.literal: Bandits accused gentry and the wealthy of communicating with the enemy and requested search and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Boxers accused local gentry and rich families of collaborating with foreigners and demanded searches and executions.

sentences.zh: 春蕃力阻，多保全。

translations.literal: Chunfan strenuously blocked this and many were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfan blocked them strenuously and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 事亟，春蕃首請召鴻章北上停戰議和。

translations.literal: When affairs were urgent Chunfan was first to request summoning Hongzhang north to halt fighting and negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis peaked he was first to urge summoning Li Hongzhang north to stop the fighting and negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 及聯軍猝至，同僚皆走，春蕃獨留不去，艱苦謀搘拄，至一月之久。

translations.literal: When the allied armies suddenly arrived colleagues all fled; Chunfan alone remained, laboring in hardship to shore up affairs for as long as a month.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies suddenly arrived his colleagues fled, but Chunfan stayed alone for a month, struggling to hold things together.

sentences.zh: 鴻章至，复參和議，約成，辭優保。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang arrived he again took part in peace talks; when the treaty was concluded he declined preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang arrived he joined the peace talks; when the treaty was signed he declined special honors.

sentences.zh: 辛亥事起，人心惶惑，春蕃夙夜籌慮，獨為地方謀保安。

translations.literal: When the xinhai affair arose popular hearts were fearful and confused; Chunfan planned day and night, alone seeking security for the locality.
translations.idiomatic: When the 1911 revolution broke out and the populace panicked, he worked day and night to keep the region secure.

sentences.zh: 焦勞益甚，猝病卒。

translations.literal: His anxiety and labor grew extreme; he suddenly fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion overtook him and he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 春蕃敦節操，有經濟才。

translations.literal: Chunfan was solid in integrity and possessed talent for statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfan was a man of integrity with real administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 自鴻章延入直幕，先後垂三十年。

translations.literal: From when Hongzhang invited him into the Zhili staff, altogether nearly thirty years passed.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Li Hongzhang brought him onto the Zhili staff, he served there for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 歷任總督如王文韶、榮祿、袁世凱、楊士驤、端方、陳夔龍等，皆敬禮之。

translations.literal: Successive governors-general such as Wang Wenshao, Ronglu, Yuan Shikai, Yang Shixiang, Duan Fang, and Chen Kuilong all treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general from Wang Wenshao and Ronglu to Yuan Shikai, Yang Shixiang, Duan Fang, and Chen Kuilong all treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 雖不樂仕進，未親吏治，而論治佐政，留意民生，各郡縣皆奉為圭臬。

translations.literal: Though he did not delight in advancement and did not personally administer, in discussing governance and assisting policy he attended to people's livelihood; every prefecture and county took him as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Though he sought no promotion and did not hold office himself, his counsel on governance and people's welfare was the standard for every prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 歿後，直人思其德，公請附祀鴻章祠。

translations.literal: After his death the people of Zhili remembered his virtue and publicly requested that he be enshrined alongside Li Hongzhang's temple.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Zhili petitioned to have him enshrined in Li Hongzhang's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：各省監司能著聲績者，大抵多起於守令，蓋親民之效焉。

translations.literal: Commentary says: provincial surveillance commissioners who achieve renown generally mostly rise from magistrates and prefects—this is the effect of closeness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes that provincial officials who win lasting renown usually began as magistrates and prefects—the fruit of serving close to the people.

sentences.zh: 及兵事興而有事功幕職，捐例開而有輸餉助賑，雖其初不必盡親吏治，而以實心行實政，流愛於人，民之感之，亦豈有異？

translations.literal: When military affairs arose there were merit-earning staff posts; when purchase offices opened there were contributions of funds to aid relief; though at first they need not all have personally administered, yet with sincere hearts practicing sincere government, spreading kindness among people—the people's response to them, how could it differ?
translations.idiomatic: When wars created staff posts for men of merit, and purchase offices brought contributors to relief work, not all had begun in routine administration; yet those who governed with sincere hearts won the people's love just the same.

sentences.zh: 自汝奎、宗濂以至錫晉、春蕃諸人，德惠在人，後人稱之至今，不可敬哉！

translations.literal: From Rukui and Zonglian down to Xijin, Chunfan, and the rest—their virtue and kindness remain among the people; later generations praise them to this day. How can one not revere them!
translations.idiomatic: From Rukui and Zonglian to Xijin and Chunfan, their kindness endures among the people and posterity still praises them. Surely they are worthy of reverence!
